claims.text: Dart has no public/protected/private/internal keywords; an identifier starting with _ is private to its library (a file plus its parts). DonHang.App/lib has no part directives at stage-4, so private means the declaring file.
claims.source_hint: dart.dev Language > Libraries & imports (privacy, 'Every Dart file is a library'); Language tour, underscore privacy

claims.text: Any Dart file under a package's lib/ can import any other file there by relative path or package: URI; a public name in catalog_api.dart such as catalogApiProvider is importable from ordering/.
claims.source_hint: dart.dev Language > Libraries & imports; dart.dev Tools > pub > package layout (lib/, relative imports)

claims.text: `export 'x.dart' show A;` re-exports only A, so a file importing the exporting library sees only the names listed with show.
claims.source_hint: dart.dev Language > Libraries & imports (show/hide combinators); Dart language specification, Exports

claims.text: At stage-4 catalog.dart exports exactly productsProvider, Product, ProductDetailScreen, ProductListScreen; catalog_api.dart (API client), product_tile.dart, product_catalog.dart and catalog_providers.dart's saved-list names are not exported.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.App/lib/features/catalog/catalog.dart lines 1-8; product_tile.dart, product_catalog.dart, catalog_providers.dart lines 19-53 @ stage-4

claims.text: create_order_screen.dart @ stage-4 imports '../catalog/catalog.dart' at line 15 (and '../auth/auth.dart' at line 11), and its build reads productsProvider through ref.watch (line 109).
In DonHang.Api, Ordering reaches products only through ICatalog; other Catalog types are internal.
Auth and Ordering also have one public file each at stage-4: features/auth/auth.dart and features/ordering/ordering.dart.

feature_boundaries_test.dart reads every .dart file under lib/ as text, matches each one-line import/export written with single quotes (conditional URIs included), resolves the target under lib/, fails once with every file:line and reason; every directive in DonHang.App/lib uses that form.
claims.source_hint: feature_boundaries_test.dart @ stage-4 lines 16-18, 24-43, 71-86; grep DonHang.App/lib for double-quoted or multi-line import/export (none)

claims.text: check(): a target outside features/ or in the same feature is allowed; shared/ or design/ using a feature fails; a target other than features/<f>/<f>.dart fails; a feature not in allowed[owner] fails; router.dart and main.dart have owner null, so only the public-file rule applies.
allowed: ordering -> {catalog, auth}; catalog -> {auth} (Catalog shows a sign-in button); auth -> {}; so no two features depend on each other.

With import '../catalog/catalog_api.dart' added after line 15 of create_order_screen.dart, the boundary test fails, listing lib/features/ordering/create_order_screen.dart:16 and 'only features/catalog/catalog.dart is public'; an Auth file importing catalog.dart gives 'auth may not use catalog'.
The ci workflow at stage-4 runs flutter test, so the boundary test runs on every pull request's CI.
A Dart package is a folder with its own pubspec.yaml, which lists the packages it depends on; DonHang.App is one package at stage-4.
claims.source_hint: dart.dev Tools > pub > The pubspec file (dependencies)

claims.text: At stage-4 one team owns the whole system, DonHang.App included (no team per feature).
claims.source_hint: docs/team/team-structure.md @ stage-4 lines 8-17 ('Đội hôm nay'); design.l4.conways-law

claims.text: Boundary test checks every file each run, review only changed files; review still judges show lists and allowed. One app per feature (separate apps placed together on screen by a piece owned by no feature) pays off when separate teams own features.

Catalog needing Ordering data should be solved on an Ordering screen or in router.dart, not by adding ordering to Catalog's allowed list (it would form a cycle, and the test would pass after that edit).
